page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core operating at 2.0 GHz across 2 threads on an x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 16 GB of memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU, and integrates 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included in this configuration.

Benchmark measurements show strong single-threaded computational capacity, with the stress-ng single-core test placing in the top ten percent and Geekbench single-core reaching 2123.0 points. Text processing in Geekbench also displays solid results at 2548.0 points. However, total multi-core processing throughput is limited by the two-vCPU count, reflected in lower scores across multi-core Geekbench and PassMark CPU evaluations. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains balanced throughput under large uncached blocks, recording 73.36 GB/sec read and 52.37 GB/sec write speeds.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with local NVMe storage provides an efficient resource profile for workloads requiring dedicated execution threads and elevated memory capacity rather than aggregate multi-threaded parallel throughput. The configuration is suited for memory-intensive background utilities, single-threaded text processing pipelines, staging environments, and moderate in-memory caching, while remaining constrained for high-concurrency database queries, static web serving throughput, or heavy multi-core compilation.

The hardware deployment includes 16 GB of system RAM, providing an 8 GB per core ratio, along with 200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a public IPv4 address without discrete GPUs. In synthetic testing, the instance demonstrates high single-core compute performance, placing in the top tiers in stress-ng single-thread tests and Geekbench text processing, though overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit. Memory throughput is consistent during large-block read and write testing. This instance configuration is suitable for memory-heavy utilities, caching, text parsing, and lightweight application hosting that prioritize individual core execution strength and RAM capacity over extensive parallel threading.
